picks.what: Woodcut in Hartmann Schedel’s Nuremberg Chronicle
picks.why: colored true view (the Romanesque cathedral is shown); two-page spread, so trimmed to the right-hand page — the town core with the cathedral, the river and the castle on its hill — to avoid the gutter

picks.what: View from the Kapuzinerberg, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 3
picks.why: colored loose sheet, high resolution: the fortress above the town and the Salzach; trimmed off the legend cartouches and figures at the bottom

picks.file: Rudolf von Alt - Ansicht von Salzburg - 1831-32.jpeg
picks.what: View over the cathedral from the Mönchsberg, painting
picks.why: color view over the cathedral domes and towers, the Kollegienkirche and the Salzach valley

picks.what: View from the Kapuzinerberg, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: the classic view: Hohensalzburg fortress over the old town, cathedral and Salzach, with snow-capped mountains; color

picks.what: The old town and the fortress, aerial photograph (ETH Library, Zurich)
picks.why: sharp oblique aerial of the old town between the Salzach and the fortress hill, cathedral and Kollegienkirche clear, Untersberg behind; portrait format

gaps: P2: nothing usable (#9 is a lake scene in Salzburg province, #12 a mountain pass, #10/#11 are the two halves of Merian’s 1644 plan). P6: no modern photographs — #27–#30 are low-resolution copies of 1890s photochroms with a 2007 upload date.
notes: #1: the Salzburg woodcut is treated as a true view (Commons files it under the Romanesque cathedral); the left page shows outlying buildings. #8: BnF dates its copy 1645; the plate first appeared in vol. 3 (1581) — #3 and #6 are vol. 3 editions, and #4 is another colored copy (its description’s ‘Bd. II, 1581’ must mean vol. 3). P1 alternative: the older Setznagel view (#5, only 1000 px), which is the Salzburg panel of the vol. 1 four-city plate of 1572 (Commons says ‘about 1575’; a high-resolution colored sheet is Ulm’s candidate #5). P3 alternatives: Jakob Alt 1844 (#15, distant view from Itzling), Sattler panorama detail of St. Peter (#14, 1829). P4 alternatives: photochrom from the fortress (#21), Adolphe Braun stereo cards 1860s (#17–#19, labeled Braun and Hogenberg by mistake).
